text:
taryn: Quick design sync — we need a "spillback" safety-net for requests when dedicated GPU pools are saturated. Goal: keep tail latency under SLO and avoid broad 429 storms for important tenants. Thinking about a two-stage fallback: 1) circuit-breaker detection, 2) tenant quota safety-net check, 3) route to backup lane (quantized or smaller model), 4) else soft-429 with suggestion header. Opinions? :thinking_face:

mike: +1 on staged approach. Couple of practical reqs: CB should be multi-signal (p99 latency + 5xx rate). Suggest thresholds: p99 > 2s OR 5xx_rate > 3% sustained for 90s => open for 2m. Also prefer same-region backup lane to avoid cross-region cost/latency.

sofia: Love the safety-net concept. Two UX asks for Console: a) per-tenant "spillback_enabled" toggle, b) preview of the fallback chain and expected token-cost delta. For routing headers, we should surface a read-only header like `x-rw-fallback-reason` so users can track why they were spilled back.

julia: Important: quota-safety-net must be tenant-aware and respect reserved capacity for Dedicated customers. If tenant has reserved QPS, we should never spill them to shared backups — instead honor their SLA or return 429 with `Retry-After`. For shared-tier tenants, spillback to quantized model is OK.

mike: Agree. Implementation sketch (gateway policy snippet):
```
policy: {
  match: { path: "/v1/generate", method: "POST" },
  triggers: {
    circuit_breaker: { p99_ms: 2000, error_rate_pct: 3, window_s: 90 },
    quota_guard: { tenant_reserved_qps: false }
  },
  fallback_chain: [
    { lane: "same-region-quant8", reason_header: "quantized-backup" },
    { lane: "shortform-llm", reason_header: "shortform-backup" },
    { action: "soft-429", reason_header: "no-capacity" }
  ]
}
```

sofia: Minor note: the gateway should attach `x-rw-fallback-destination: same-region-quant8` and `x-rw-fallback-reason: circuit-breaker` when we route. That makes downstream observability and eval easier.

ares: We should also add a low-cost probe run to the primary model while spillback is active so we can detect recovery quickly (sample ~1% of traffic routed to primary but with low priority). This avoids long cold-open CB windows. Add a tag `spillback_probe` to traces.

julia: +1 on probe. Keep probe size configurable per-tenant in Console. Also add a metric `spillback_probe_success_rate` and alert if > 80% for 5m -> consider closing CB automatically.

mike: Caveat: when we probe, ensure KV cache heat is isolated — don't warm the primary model's KV for full requests from probe traffic. Probe should be truncated tokens or synthetic prompts.

sofia: Console rollout UX: expose a "simulate spillback" toggle in staging that shows the fallback path, headers emitted, and projected cost delta. Helps SREs and customer success reproduce customer reports.

taryn: This looks actionable. Next steps: 1) implement gateway policy parser for `fallback_chain` and `reason_header`, 2) add headers to route output, 3) add probe runner in runtime with sampling config, 4) Console flags + metric panels. I'll open issues.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for `spillback-probe` feature to staging cluster `stg-west-02` (build: rwd-infer-2026.03.18-canary).

mike: I'll pick up gateway parser PR. Sofia/Julia — can you draft Console mocks for the toggle and metrics?

sofia: Yep, will drop a Loom and Figma by EOD.

taryn: Thanks all. If we agree on thresholds above I'll file the RFC and link the Console mocks. :thumbsup:
